memories.content: Conduct one review prior to submission focusing solely on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.
Cross-check whether research questions align with the core functions of the prototype.
Cross-check whether evaluation tasks align with representative measures.
Cross-check whether collected evidence aligns with design and operational decisions to be changed.
Verify at the end that user problems, design interventions, user studies, and expected contributions form a coherent logical flow.
HCI reviewers view the validity of design interventions as low if research questions are not linked to prototype functions.
HCI reviewers view the validity of evaluation plans as low if evaluation tasks do not produce representative measures.
HCI reviewers view the practicality of contributions as low if collected evidence cannot change design or operational decisions.
Cross-check at the end whether each research question, formative evaluation data, and design modification judgment are seamlessly connected.
Review whether the application conditions of proposed design principles and boundary cases of failure are presented together.
The user can have contributions reviewed only if prototype outcomes and the transferable design knowledge derived from them are separated.
The scope of observation in controlled formative evaluations does not include long-term adaptation and operational changes in real-world usage contexts.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: Both frames support stronger research-question traceability and a clearer separation between prototype features and transferable contributions. The reference emphasizes submission-stage logical validity and evaluation limits, while the compared frame adds field-data planning, preregistration, bounded-target budgeting, deployment risks, and safety precedence.

relations.reason: The claims govern complementary links needed to establish the validity and answerability of research questions without requiring a scope distinction.
relations.summary: Research questions should be traceable both to prototype functions and to specified data sources and analysis procedures.

relations.reason: One frame requires separating prototype outcomes from transferable knowledge, while the other identifies the authoring tendency that this separation addresses.
relations.summary: Implemented prototype features or outcomes should not be presented directly as transferable design contributions.

relations.reason: Only the reference specifies this review timing, frequency, and restricted focus.
relations.summary: A single pre-submission review should focus exclusively on the validity of user problems, design interventions, and evaluation logic.

relations.reason: Only the reference states this task-to-measure validity requirement and its reviewer consequence.
relations.summary: Evaluation tasks should produce representative measures so that the evaluation plan is judged valid.

relations.reason: Only the reference connects evidence to actionable design or operational changes and contribution practicality.
relations.summary: Collected evidence should be capable of changing design or operational decisions to support practical contributions.

relations.reason: These reference memories express complementary parts of one end-stage coherence check.
relations.summary: A final coherence check should connect research questions, user evidence or studies, design modifications, and expected contributions into a logical flow.

relations.reason: Only the reference requires explicit conditions and failure boundaries for design principles.
relations.summary: Proposed design principles should present their application conditions together with boundary cases of failure.

relations.reason: Only the reference defines this limitation on the observation scope of controlled formative evaluation.
relations.summary: Controlled formative evaluations do not observe long-term adaptation or operational change in real-world use.

relations.reason: These compared memories split the instrumentation and timing components of one data-collection specification.
relations.summary: Field and user data plans should identify collection instruments and when collection occurs relative to deployment.

relations.reason: These compared memories state complementary components of one plan-change documentation policy.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should specify both the criteria for judging plan changes and where those changes are recorded.

relations.reason: The compared memories collectively define and justify one operational policy for non-arbitrary target ranges and their tradeoffs.
relations.summary: When confirmations may change, use a justified bounded target whose minimum and maximum have explicit deliverables, workload, schedule, and budget consequences while acknowledging residual uncertainty.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame identifies infrastructure instability as an independent failure cause.
relations.summary: Field-deployment task failures may arise independently from network or service instability rather than design choices.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame establishes this safety override.
relations.summary: A field-system safety signal makes institutional safety procedures take precedence over research schedules and data collection plans.

reports.both: Both require traceable research questions and distinguish implemented prototype features from transferable design contributions.
reports.compared_only: The compared frame adds field-data collection details, preregistered change documentation, operationally justified target ranges, infrastructure-related failure causes, and institutional safety precedence.
reports.reference_only: The reference adds final coherence checks, representative evaluation measures, decision-relevant evidence, design-principle boundaries, and limits of controlled formative evaluation.
